mappings.note: Names the executive as the organ of head of state and ministers that implements laws - an organ-to-function item, so LO-219.
Matches foreign affairs to the Central Government against state and local distractors; a tier-identification item, hence LO-220.
Parliament as the maker of a national internet law - identifying the union legislature, so LO-220.

Assertion that citizens elect representatives because direct participation is impractical (CG-SST3), with the printed answer turning on national currency being a central rather than local function (LO-220). The item's text is mixed, so both strands are cited.
Sorts making, implementing and interpreting laws among the three organs and rejects the swapped claims - an organ-to-function item, so LO-219.
One party holding legislature, executive and judiciary: the missing principle is separation of powers, which concerns how government is built (LO-219) and safeguards citizens' rights (CG-SST3).
Names representative democracy as the system where elected officials legislate for citizens - a question about the form of democracy, so the goal.

School rules for discipline, safety and orderly learning. The chapter uses such rules as the step towards laws and governance, so LO-219 is the nearest honest fit; no outcome covers school rules as such.
Checks and balances preventing misuse of power - a structural feature of government (LO-219) that protects the democratic order (CG-SST3).
Supreme Court against High Court: the judiciary as an organ (LO-219) at two different levels of the system (LO-220).
The legislature as the law-making organ; an organ-to-function item, so LO-219.
The executive as the implementing organ - the companion item to the legislature question, under the same outcome.
The judiciary as the system of courts deciding whether laws are broken; the third organ-to-function item.
The purpose of separating powers, namely checks and balances - a point about how government is constructed, so LO-219.
What follows if one group holds all three organs: abuse of power. Structure of government (LO-219) and the democratic values at risk (CG-SST3).
Flood response at different scales showing each level has its own part - explicitly about local, state and union roles, so LO-220.
Satyameva Jayate as the national motto; a symbol of the constitutional order, so CG-SST3. Not LO-225, since the item asks whose motto it is, not what the Upanishadic idea means.
Yato Dharmastato Jayah as the Supreme Court's motto: a constitutional symbol (CG-SST3) belonging to the judicial organ (LO-219).
Executive enforcing against legislature making - the clearest organ-to-function discrimination in the batch, so LO-219.
Rules out national foreign policy from state functions, keeping police, agriculture and education; a tier-of-government item, so LO-220.
The Prime Minister as real executive head with the Council of Ministers: the executive organ (LO-219) at the union level (LO-220), against the President's nominal headship.
Rules as what becomes necessary when many people live together - the ground on which governance rests, so LO-219.
Governance as deciding, organising and enforcing; the short-answer twin of the definition item.
Government as the body that makes and enforces rules - the companion definition, under LO-219.
Laws as the more important rules a government makes; the vocabulary of the government's role.
Defines cybercrime, the example the chapter uses for new law-making. It sits with the government's law-making role, so LO-219.
The legislature as the organ that makes and updates laws - the short-answer form of the organ-to-function item.
That the legislature's work is done by an assembly of the people's representatives: the organ (LO-219) and the representative principle behind it (CG-SST3).
The executive as the implementing organ; short-answer twin of the multiple-choice version.
Separation of powers existing to give checks and balances - a structural point about government, so LO-219.
Three tiers of government in India; the plainest LO-220 item in the chapter.
The national tier named Central or Union government - identifying a level, so LO-220.
Recalls Satyameva Jayate as the Government of India's motto; a symbol of the constitutional order, hence CG-SST3.
Translates Satyameva Jayate as 'truth alone triumphs' - the meaning of the national motto, mapped with the recall item.
Recalls the Supreme Court's motto: a constitutional symbol (CG-SST3) of the judicial organ (LO-219).
Translates Yato Dharmastato Jayah - the meaning of the court's motto, so the same pair as the recall version.
Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha as the two national houses; identifying the union legislature, so LO-220.
The President as nominal head of the Central Government - an office of the union tier, hence LO-220.
Asks who is the executive head of the Central Government; the printed answer text is corrupted by page furniture, but the question itself is a clean union-tier item, so LO-220.

A damaged item: the stem repeats the executive-head question but the answer supplied is about the chaos that follows if nobody keeps the rules. Mapped on the answered content - why rules and their enforcement matter, which is LO-219.
